purpose: Accessibility, visual-state, search/navigation, and data-quality presentation cases

cases.userFriction: Users who are sensitive to motion must still understand timeline transitions without animation-dependent meaning.
Keyboard users should not be locked out of the product's primary history exploration surface.
Dense visualizations need a meaningful non-visual interpretation rather than an empty accessibility tree.

cases.scenario: Tracking gap visually distinguishable from zero activity
cases.userFriction: Users should never need to guess whether blank means no usage or missing data.
High-resolution events should remain inspectable without becoming impossible to click or understand.
Renaming should not orphan historical usage or make search feel inconsistent.

cases.scenario: Search finds historical page title only when title collection is enabled
cases.userFriction: Privacy controls should affect search predictably as well as storage.
The user should understand the tracker failed rather than conclude they used nothing.
Comparing a partial day to a full day without context can make perfectly normal numbers look alarming.
Analytics may temporarily lag while tracking is healthy; users should see the distinction instead of assuming data loss.
